transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I came in because for the past few weeks I’ve just felt really down… like there’s this heavy sadness sitting on me most of the day. Even at work, I’ll be smiling and talking with patients, but inside I feel like I’m barely holding it together.
Did this low mood start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?
Yeah… it started about three weeks ago, shortly after I found out I was pregnant. That’s when I really noticed my mood getting low.
Do you feel that finding out you were pregnant is what caused your sadness?
It seems connected, yeah. It’s been going on about three weeks, starting shortly after I found out I was pregnant.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
Yeah. I used to paint after work, or go to yoga or salsa to unwind, but lately I just… don’t. I go home, sit on the couch, and ignore texts. None of it feels worth the effort right now.
Since you found out you were pregnant, has that been feeling very stressful or hard to cope with?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. It’s been a lot to take in, but I don’t know if I’d describe it as the main thing I’m struggling to cope with.
Before this pregnancy, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed like this?
I’m not sure. I mean, I’ve had rough periods before, like anyone, but I don’t know that I’ve felt depressed in this same way before.
Do you feel your sadness is mainly a reaction to being pregnant?
I don’t know that I can say it’s mainly because of the pregnancy. I mean, it’s part of what’s going on, but the sadness feels bigger than just that.
Have you been feeling worthless or guilty lately?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I’d say I feel worthless exactly. I do feel bad about myself sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s guilt or just feeling low.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid close attention to it, I guess. I don’t know that I’ve noticed a clear change.
Before you found out you were pregnant, had you been feeling down or depressed most days for a long time?
No, not really for a long time before that. It’s been more like about three weeks, since shortly after I found out I was pregnant.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite lately?

Yeah, my appetite’s definitely been off. I know I should be eating regularly, especially being pregnant, but most days food just doesn’t sound good. I’ll be halfway through a clinic shift and realize I’ve only had crackers or coffee all day.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

Yeah… I have had thoughts like I wish I just wouldn’t wake up. That’s honestly what scared me enough to say something at my prenatal appointment. I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but the thoughts have been there.
Have you been having trouble concentrating lately?

Yeah, I have. My brain just feels foggy. At work I keep having to reread medication orders and wound-care notes because they don’t stick the first time. And decisions I normally make without thinking now make me freeze up and second-guess myself.
Before this pregnancy, was there ever a time in your life when you felt this same kind of depression for at least two weeks?
I’m not really sure. I’ve had stressful periods before where I felt down, but I don’t know that it was ever like this for two weeks straight before the pregnancy.
Before this pregnancy, was there ever a time when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I don’t think so. I’ve had times where I was stressed or down for a bit, but I can’t remember a time before this pregnancy where it was most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks like you’re asking.
Have you felt noticeably slowed down lately, like your body or movements are moving in slow motion?
Yes. Everything feels slowed down, like I’m moving through syrup. Even simple things at the clinic—like getting wound supplies together or finishing my charting—take me a lot longer than they should.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy lately?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I feel worn out a lot, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether it’s more than usual or just from everything going on.
Has this depression made it hard for you to function in your daily life?

Yes. I’m still getting myself to work, but it’s been harder to keep up. My supervisor has noticed my charting isn’t always finished, and I’ve been pulling away from friends and from the things that usually help me stay steady.
Before this pregnancy, was there ever a time when you had the same kind of symptoms you’re having now for at least two weeks in a row?
I’m not sure. I don’t really have a clear time before this where I can say it was the same and lasted at least two weeks.
Before this pregnancy, had you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you lost interest in most things you usually enjoy?

Not really before the pregnancy, no. What I’m noticing is more lately—after my shifts I used to paint or go to yoga or salsa to unwind, and now I mostly just go home, sit on the couch, and ignore texts because none of it feels worth the effort.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for a current major depressive episode with severe features: depressed mood, marked anhedonia, decreased appetite, suicidal ideation (passive death wish), impaired concentration, psychomotor retardation, and functional impairment for about 3 weeks. Although symptoms began after learning of pregnancy, the patient did not clearly describe the mood state as primarily a stress reaction, and the syndrome is more consistent with a major depressive episode than adjustment disorder. Prior qualifying depressive episodes were not established, so recurrent depressive disorder is not supported.
